question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=8x-{x}^{4}$ and the point $P(1,7)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(7,1)$ is$\,${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(1,7).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =8x-{x}^{4} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =8-4{x}^{3} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(1,7)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(7,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(7) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(7))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
